A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same gradient-stabilization study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments, RL simulations, gradient diagnostics and architecture/optimizer comparisons across CIFAR-10, ALE, Isaac Gym and DMC.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds offline RL evaluations, a skip-count ablation and additional stabilization comparisons.

M1.justification: The proposed encoder-to-MLP multi-skip connections and Kron optimization remain unchanged. Applying these interventions to offline algorithms and testing ablated variants does not introduce a revised proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Figure 11 adds four offline RL tasks: Cube Octuple Play, Humanoidmaze Giant Navigate, and Puzzle 4x5/4x6 Play. This substantially extends v1's classification and online RL coverage to learning from fixed datasets across manipulation, navigation and puzzle tasks.

E2.justification: Figure 11 introduces comparisons with ten original offline algorithms, including DSHARSA, SHARSA and GC-IQL. Table 3 adds activation, regularization, scheduler and learning-rate alternatives. The earlier RAdam, AdaBelief, Shampoo and Apollo comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix C.5 adds a controlled evaluation holding a large five-block network fixed while varying encoder connections to the first one through five blocks. C.7 adds learning-rate and scheduler controls. Previously reported model configurations, budgets and hyperparameter tables remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Tables 2–3 substantially expand the analyses: the skip-count ablation tests the value of broadcasting encoder features throughout the network, while activation, regularization and learning-rate comparisons test alternative stabilization strategies. These supplement the retained optimizer and scaling analyses.

E5.justification: New checklist item 7 explicitly describes confidence intervals and standard deviations in training curves and percentiles in boxplots. This is a reporting clarification; the existing three-seed ALE, five-seed DMC and 95% bootstrap-interval reporting remains, with no documented increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds offline outcomes and extensive ablation scores. New Table 2 reports aggregate mean Atari-10 HNS rising from 0.25 with one encoder skip to 0.58 with five; Table 3 reports alternative-intervention scores. The retained ALE median relative improvements remain 83.27% for PQN and 31.40% for PPO.

T1.justification: The gradient-propagation equations, variance assumptions and curvature-based update explanation are retained. No new theorem, proof, substantive derivation or formal definition is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same central diagnosis and contribution: gradient pathologies interact with non-stationarity, and architectural and optimizer interventions enable stable scaling. Additional experiments support this contribution without redefining the central claims.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly interprets offline benefits as complementary to horizon reduction and applicable with stationary inputs. Appendices C.5–C.7 strengthen the rationale for full encoder broadcasting and the selected interventions. Existing mechanism explanations and computational limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents the five-block, first-k skip-ablation implementation and explains the default-hyperparameter policy. Existing hyperparameter tables, hardware and timings are retained. Both PDFs link the same repository, but v2 adds a conflicting checklist statement promising future code release; offline training configurations remain sparsely documented.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused positioning relative to Park et al.'s horizon-reduction approach and citations supporting alternative plasticity/stabilization methods. Section 6 adds recent neuronal-activity and sparsity work while retaining its original gradient-flow positioning.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative remain intact. v2 adds Section 4.4 and offline discussion, separates appendix subsections, moves ALE/DMC results to E.1–E.2, and adds broader-impact and checklist material alongside citation and author-information edits.

P2.justification: The document adopts NeurIPS formatting with extensive changes to typography, captions, spacing and figure/table placement. Figure 11 and Tables 2–3 are added, appendix displays are reorganized, and some plot axes are relabeled. Most existing graphical results are reused.

improvement.justification: The controlled skip-count ablation and broader alternative-intervention comparisons strengthen the justification for an already extensively evaluated design. Offline experiments add useful applicability evidence. Sparse offline configuration details, mixed offline outcomes, and inconsistent learning-rate values between C.7 and Table 3 limit the strength of the expanded conclusions.
